# Druidcraft: The Whisper of the Wilds

To the uninitiated, *Druidcraft* appears a mere parlor trick—a bud blooming out of season or a sudden scent of pine. Yet, to the practitioner, it is the foundational heartbeat of the Green. When one shapes the Weave into this cantrip, it does not feel like the sharp, intellectual snap of wizardry. instead, it is a slow, rhythmic thrum against the palms—the "Sap-Pulse"—as if the very lifeblood of the world is surging through your veins.

Visually, it is subtle but profound. A caster might summon a miniature thunderhead that smells of impending rain or cause a seed to split and sprout in a heartbeat. It is the magic of the mundane, elevated to the divine.

### The Legend of the First Sprout
Elders claim the first Druid, Caelen of the Deep Root, discovered this art not through study, but through grief. In a valley turned to ash by dragonfire, Caelen knelt and hummed a song of mourning. The earth, recognizing the vibration of life, pushed a single clover through the soot to meet his hand. He did not command the plant; he simply invited it to exist.
